task_commit_basis: merge commit of the reference change (code after the optimization landed), from https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/c23b2a4468a45f0a11820e3ad8597ac1e3ac19eb

workload.command: bundle exec ruby --yjit -C activesupport -Ilib -e "require 'active_support'; require 'active_support/time'; t = Time.utc(2026, 1, 1).in_time_zone('Eastern Time (US & Canada)'); 300_000.times { t.xmlschema; t.to_s; ActiveSupport::TimeZone.seconds_to_utc_offset(-18000) }"
workload.source: adapted from the benchmark-ips script in the description of https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/58751 (TimeWithZone#xmlschema and #to_s on a non-UTC zone, and TimeZone.seconds_to_utc_offset, under YJIT)

oracle.source: Active Support's TimeWithZone and TimeZone tests (both changed by https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/58751); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 3.10x; 2.70x; 1.20x; 1.78x; 1.96x | timings: 100ms; 654.61 ns; 5.065034s; 210.99 ns; 5.061557s; 704.20 ns; 5.028475s; 260.33 ns

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. Runs natively with CRuby 4.0.9 and Bundler 4.0.20 that the eval user has in ~/.local/ruby (docs/evaluation.md, T3.8), so the runtime gate identifies it. Gems are the tree's Gemfile.lock, installed into $HOME/.bundle-gems (the tree's HOME, set in bundler's global config), without the rubocop, mdl, doc, job, cable, storage and db groups (the db group builds pg, mysql2 and trilogy, which need client libraries this Mac does not have, and Active Support does not use them). The commands start in the tree root, so Ruby changes into activesupport itself (ruby -C) where the Docker form used -w /src/activesupport. The sqlite3 gem is built against the SDK's sqlite (BUNDLE_BUILD__SQLITE3=--enable-system-libraries): bundler did not pick the lockfile's prebuilt arm64-darwin gem for Ruby 4.0.9, and the source build with the gem's own sqlite stopped for want of pkg-config, which this Mac does not have
